w: A Church of England parish church with roots to the 12th century, and possibly the very church recorded in the Domesday Book's Mortlake Hundred. Still in active use today, it has held Grade II* listed status since 1949 - a rare survival of medieval worship at the heart of Wimbledon village.
s: Possibly a Domesday-Book church, Grade II* since 1949
_facts: Has existed since the 12th century
Possibly the church recorded in the Domesday Book (Mortlake Hundred)
Grade II* listed since 1949
Still an active parish church

w: The first purpose-built mosque in London, opened in 1926 in Southfields after Ahmadi Muslim women in Qadian, Punjab, funded its 6,223-pound construction. From 1984 to 2019 it housed the Ahmadiyya Caliphs, making it the movement's de facto world headquarters before that role moved to Tilford.
_facts: Opened 3 October 1926
First purpose-built mosque in London
Funded by Ahmadi Muslim women in Qadian, Punjab, at a cost of 6,223 pounds
Was residence of the Ahmadiyya Caliphs 1984-2019

w: 460 hectares of heath and woodland across three named areas - Wimbledon Common, Putney Heath and Putney Lower Common - managed jointly as Wimbledon and Putney Commons. Putney Lower Common sits apart, separated from the rest by over a mile of the built-up western edge of Putney.
s: 460 hectares of common land across three linked areas
_facts: 460 hectares (1,140 acres) in total
Comprises Wimbledon Common, Putney Heath and Putney Lower Common
Putney Lower Common is separated by over a mile of built-up Putney

w: A 27-hectare park that gives its name to the surrounding suburb and its tube station, sitting immediately east of the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club. Despite the shared name it is a separate space from Wimbledon Common, which lies further west, up the hill.
s: 27-hectare park beside the All England Club
_facts: 27 hectares (67 acres) in area
Adjoins the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club
Distinct from Wimbledon Common, further west up the hill

w: Britain's first large-scale carbon-neutral housing scheme, built in Hackbridge on the edge of Sutton. Designed from the outset to create zero net carbon emissions, BedZED proved that eco-housing could work as a whole community, not just as a one-off show home.
s: Britain's first large-scale zero-carbon housing estate
_facts: Located in Hackbridge, London Borough of Sutton
Designed to create zero carbon emissions
First large-scale community built to this standard

w: A Grade II listed Edwardian theatre on the Broadway, opened in 1910 with the pantomime Jack and Jill and fitted with what may be Britain's only theatre-basement Turkish bath. Gracie Fields, Noel Coward and Sybil Thorndike all played here, and Lionel Bart's Oliver! had its world premiere on this stage in 1960.
s: Edwardian theatre where Oliver! had its world premiere
_facts: Opened 26 December 1910 with the pantomime Jack and Jill
Grade II listed, designed by Cecil Aubrey Massey and Roy Young
Possibly the only British theatre with a basement Turkish bath
World premiere of Lionel Bart's Oliver! in 1960

w: A 3.2-hectare triangle of grassland and woodland in Mitcham, bounded by Cranmer Road, King George VI Avenue and a railway line. Named after the Cranmer family, local from 1761 to 1843, its pond likely dates to the late eighteenth century and survives as a Site of Local Importance for Nature Conservation.
s: Local nature reserve named after the Cranmer family
_facts: 3.2 hectares, a Site of Local Importance for Nature Conservation
Named after the Cranmer family, local from 1761 to 1843
Pond probably dates to the late 18th century

w: The largest tennis museum in the world, opened inside the All England Club's grounds in 2006 by the Duke of Kent. Exhibits span from 1555 to the present, including touchscreen consoles and seasonal memorabilia from Victorian champions to today's players, and guided Blue Badge tours go behind the scenes.
s: World's largest tennis museum, inside the All England Club
_facts: Opened to the public 12 April 2006 by the Duke of Kent
Largest tennis museum in the world
Exhibits date back to 1555
Open to ticket holders only during Championships week
